newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's Berisha, parties agree to halt army action.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Berisha, parties agree to halt army action.

text.p: President Sali Berisha, backed by Albania's opposition parties, agreed on Thursday to suspend military activity against rebels in the south and to offer an amnesty to insurgents who surrendered weapons within two days.

A statement issued by the president and 10 parties after more than five hours of talks also said Berisha would seek a political consensus on replacing Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi, who stepped down last weekend.

The statement said participants asked the Council of Defence, overseeing emergency measures introduced last weekend, "to order the suspension of offensive military operations in the zones where they had been planned, for 48 hours starting at 6 a.m. (0500 GMT) on Friday."
Insurgents were to start turning in weapons at the same time and would be offered an amnesty if they had committed no crimes.

The statement, signed by Berisha's Democratic Party and nine opposition groups, said Berisha would "start consultations for the appointment of a new prime minister aiming at the greatest possible consensus."
Signatories "supported the restoration of constitutional order and guaranteeing public order throughout the country."
The Socialists, the backbone of the Forum for Democracy opposition alliance, made no comment on the accord.

But a top Social Democrat, Paskal Milo, said the talks had achieved nothing as Berisha had yet to agree to the principle of a coalition government as demanded by his opponents and Western countries. His party signed the agreement merely to calm the situation in the south, he said.

More than 25 people have died in southern Albania in the latest wave of more than a month of violence, most in the port of Vlore, focal point of anger last month by penniless investors after the collapse of pyramid investment funds.
Rebels control several towns in the south and some have threatened to remain dug in until Berisha resigns.
Opposition parties have demanded the creation of a coalition government of technocrats.
The statement called for an all-party commission of experts to investigate the demise of the pyramid schemes, in which hundreds of thousands of Albanians lost their life savings.

International efforts to find a political solution to the crisis intensified. A Council of Europe delegation was in Tirana and Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo, representing the European Union, was due to arrive on Friday after talks in Rome and Athens.
